questions.question: The Indian National Congress was established when 72 delegates from all over the country met at Bombay in December ________.
questions.solution:
1885 was the founding year of the Indian National Congress. First Session:
  • Held at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay.
  • President: W.C. Bonnerjee.
  • Founder: A.O. Hume.

questions.question: In 1867, Keshab Chunder Sen helped found the Prarthana Samaj in ______.
questions.solution: Bombay was where the Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1867. Founders: Atmaram Pandurang with help from Keshab Chandra Sen. It focused on social reforms like widow remarriage and education.

questions.question: The iron pillar is situated in which of the following places?
questions.solution: Delhi (Mehrauli) is the location of the famous Iron Pillar. Highlight: Built during the Gupta period (Chandragupta II), it is world-famous for its rust-resistant properties.

questions.question: Which foreign invader surrendered his territories to Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution: Seleucus Nicator surrendered his territories (Aria, Arachosia, Gedrosia) to Chandragupta Maurya after his defeat. Megasthenes was sent as an ambassador to the Maurya court.

questions.question: Who among the following succeeded the throne of the Mauryan Empire after the death of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution: Bindusara succeeded Chandragupta Maurya. Titles: Known to the Greeks as 'Amitrochates' (Slayer of Foes). He was the father of Emperor Ashoka.

questions.question: Who among the following Navratnas from Chandragupta II court wrote 'Mantrashastra'?
questions.solution: Vetala Bhatta was one of the Navratnas (Nine Gems) in the court of Chandragupta II who wrote the Mantrashastra. Other Gems: Kalidasa, Varahmihira, Amarasimha.

questions.question: When was the Treaty of Purandar signed between Jai Singh I, commander of the Mughal Empire, and Shivaji?
questions.solution: 1665 was the year the Treaty of Purandar was signed. Parties: Jai Singh I (representing Mughals) and Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. Shivaji had to surrender 23 forts.

questions.question: As per the contents mentioned in Asokan inscriptions, how many major political centres were there in the Mauryan empire?
questions.solution: Five major political centres were mentioned: Pataliputra (capital) and four provincial centres: Taxila, Ujjayini, Tosali, and Suvarnagiri.

questions.question: Provida style of architecture belongs to which empire?
questions.solution: Vijayanagar Empire is famous for the Provida/Vijayanagara style. Characteristics: Tall Raya Gopurams, carved pillars with Yali (mythical creatures), and Kalyanmandapas.

questions.question: The Ahom Kingdom in India was located in the _______
questions.solution: Brahmaputra valley in present-day Assam was the seat of the Ahom Kingdom. They ruled for 600 years and successfully resisted Mughal expansion (Battle of Saraighat).

questions.question: There were several cities in the Maurya empire. Which of the following cities was located on the southernmost side?
questions.solution: Brahmagiri was the southernmost major city/site mentioned in Mauryan inscriptions, located in modern-day Karnataka. Note: Ashoka's edicts are found here.

questions.question: The term “Vetti” in Chola empire is related to __________.
questions.solution: Forced labour was known as 'Vetti' in the Chola administration. Taxation: 'Kadamai' was the land revenue tax. The Cholas were known for their Village Self-Government.

questions.question: The kingdoms of Chola, Chera and Pandyas belong to which period in the ancient India?
questions.solution: Sangam Period refers to the era of the three great Tamil dynasties: Cheras, Cholas, and Pandyas. Literature: The era is named after the 'Sangam' assemblies of poets.

questions.question: Which of the following reforms led to the enactment of the Government of India Act of 1919?
questions.solution: Montagu-Chelmsford reforms led to the Government of India Act 1919. Key Feature: Introduction of Diarchy (dual government) in the provinces.

questions.question: Which of the following personality is associated with Aligarh movement?
questions.solution: Syed Ahmed Khan founded the Aligarh Movement to promote modern education among Muslims. Institution: He established the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College (now AMU) in 1875.

questions.question: Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das gave up their legal practices during which Movement?
questions.solution: <u>Non-Cooperation Movement</u> (1920-22) saw many leaders like Motilal Nehru and C.R. Das boycott British courts and give up their lucrative legal practices.

questions.question: In 1927, B.R Ambedkar started which movement with Dalits?
questions.solution: Temple entry movement was started by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in 1927 at the Kalaram Temple in Nashik. Purpose: To fight against the exclusion of Dalits from religious places.

questions.question: Annie Besant was associated with which of the following socio-religious movement?
questions.solution: Theosophical Society was joined by Annie Besant in England; she later became its president and settled in India. Headquarters: Adyar (Madras).

questions.question: When was the 2nd battle of Tarain fought?
questions.solution: 1192 was the year of the Second Battle of Tarain where Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan, marking the start of Muslim rule in India.

questions.question: The Third Battle of Panipat took place in ________.
questions.solution: <u>1761</u> was the year the Third Battle of Panipat took place. It severely weakened the Maratha power and cleared the path for British supremacy.

questions.question: The Third Battle of Panipat was fought between _______.
questions.solution: Marathas and Afghans (led by Ahmad Shah Abdali) fought the Third Battle of Panipat. The Marathas were led by Sadashivrao Bhau.

questions.question: Which Sultan was defeated by Babur in the first battle of Panipat 1526?
questions.solution: Ibrahim Lodi was the Sultan of Delhi defeated by Babur in the First Battle of Panipat (1526). Babur used artillery (canons) for the first time in North India.

questions.question: What was the title given to the late Sarojini Naidu?
questions.solution: <u>Nightingale of India</u> (Bharat Kokila) is the title given to Sarojini Naidu for her lyrical and patriotic poetry.

questions.question: Ritusamhara or The Six Seasons is a classic of Sanskrit literature, written by ________.
questions.solution:
Kalidasa wrote the Ritusamhara. Other works:
  • Abhigyanashakuntalam (Play)
  • Meghaduta (Poem)
  • Kumarasambhava (Epic)

questions.question: Which among the following freedom fighters is regarded as the "Father of Modern India"?
questions.solution: Raja Ram Mohan Roy is called the 'Father of Modern India' or the 'Prophet of Indian Nationalism' for his efforts in social and educational reform.
